instruction: Create a new sheet in the 'Employee Performance Evaluation Summary' Excel file named 'Quality Summary'. In this sheet, create a summary table showing the count of employees for each rating level (Unsatisfactory, Satisfactory, Good, Excellent) in the 'Quality of Work' category. Use column A for rating names and column B for counts. Save the file.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies all 4 rating levels (Excellent, Good, Satisfactory, Unsatisfactory) with correct expected counts including Unsatisfactory: 0.
Correct sheet name verification: Getter checks for exact match 'Quality Summary' (line 35-36 in getters/xlsx.py), ensuring the sheet is named exactly as required.

Proper metric logic: Metric correctly handles expected parameter (when type='rule', expected IS the rules dict), accesses expected_counts directly, and verifies all expected ratings are present in result.

Appropriate completeness check: Metric returns 0.0 if any expected rating is missing from result (line 39-41), ensuring the summary table contains all required ratings.
Minor assumption: Getter starts reading from row 2 (line 45), assuming row 1 is a header. This is a reasonable assumption for summary tables but could miss data if user doesn't add headers.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding error handling or flexible row detection in getter to handle cases where the user doesn't add a header row (though this is a minor edge case for a 'summary table' which typically has headers).
